newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures surged to a contract high for the second day in succession amid a mood of general euphoria after a market-favourable U.S. election result and a series of bullish 1997 economic forecasts from the EU.

The December bond future hit its high for the day in the first hour of the session before profit taking set in. But while many traders had expected a larger selloff, steady buying by several French brokerages buoyed the contract.
Traders said any interest from investors had waned after the initial activity and that Thursday's OAT auction could put some pressure on prices tomorrow morning.
"To be honest it's not really been active this afternoon, we're just lacking interest," said the head of futures trading at a French brokerage.

He said some of the primary dealers were a little nervous ahead of the OAT sale and had begun to sell contracts to cover potential losses. However he said a cautious approach was hardly surprising with prices at their highest level this year.
Some traders said the gap left between 127.04 and 127.18 could well be the first target on Thursday morning although the tone of the U.S. bond market overnight would be crucial.

Ciaran O'Hagan, bond analyst at JP Morgan in Paris, said Thursday's auction would have relatively little impact as the Treasury would be selling the TEC 10 variable rate OAT and the 8.25 percent 2004 OAT, as well as the benchmark 10-year bond.
"It's not a big size and the TEC and 2004 will have almost no duration impact on the market," O'Hagan said. "That just leaves six or seven billion of the 2006."
Another analyst at a French bank said the TEC would probably attract the most interest and the 2004 bond would attract interest as the cheapest to deliver bond for the December bond futures contract.

The CADES welfare debt repayment fund also announced it will be tapping its three existing French franc bonds, maturing in 2002, 2005 and 2007, with an auction next November 13, in line with expectations.

The futures contract fell to its low for the day after the European Monetary Institute said "strong and sustained action is needed to improve the fiscal position" ahead of planned European monetary monetary union in 1999.
Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro in Paris, said the EMI was probably criticising the use of a transfer of funds from France Telecom to cut the French deficit in 1997.
"But I'm not sure France is lagging in the fiscal process ... Definitely strong action has been taken, certainly the bulk has been done from mid-1995 to mid-1996," Brossard said.
The EMI report was released soon after the European Union Commisssion said 12 out of 15 member countries would meet the Maastrict Treaty targets in 1997.
"The report was bullish, it added to the general euphoria," said O'Hagan at JP Morgan.
The franc remained relatively stable on Wednesday and was trading at 3.3790 per mark late in the day, little changed from 3.3786 late on Tuesday.

December PIBOR remained in positive territory, matching its contract high at 96.49 early in the session. One trader said there had been steady profit-taking at the front end of the PIBOR strip, notably in the March contract, ever since the Bank of France cut the intervention rate last Thursday.
The most active options contract on the bond future was the 128 call, with a volume of more than 13,000 contracts. The most traded put was the 126 contract.
